question: According to the Census of India 2011, which group of states recorded the lowest male literacy rate?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar and Arunachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Census of India 2011, Bihar and Arunachal Pradesh recorded the lowest male literacy rates among all the states in India.
 
• The male literacy rate in Bihar was significantly low compared to the national average.
 
• Arunachal Pradesh, while having a relatively low male literacy rate, also faced challenges with its geographical and socio-economic conditions affecting education.
 
• Efforts have been made by both state and central governments to improve literacy rates in these states through various educational schemes and programs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Literacy Rate:**

 
 
• Literacy rate is the percentage of people who are able to read and write in a given population. It is an important indicator of the educational level of a region.
 
• The Census of India collects data on literacy rates every ten years.
 
 
 
• **Census of India 2011:**
 
 
• The Census of India 2011 was the 15th National Census of the country since 1872.
 
• It was conducted in two phases: House listing and Housing Census, and Population Enumeration.
 
• Data collected included demographics, literacy, education, and many other socio-economic parameters.
 
 
 
• **Educational Programs:**
 
 
• Various educational programs have been initiated by the Indian government to improve literacy rates, such as Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA), Mid-Day Meal Scheme, and National Literacy Mission.
 
• These programs aim to provide free and compulsory education to children up to a certain age and improve the quality of education.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Education:**
 
 
• States like Bihar and Arunachal Pradesh face unique challenges such as poverty, socio-economic barriers, and geographical constraints that affect the reach and quality of education.
 
• Addressing these challenges requires targeted interventions and sustained efforts from both government and non-governmental organizations.
